highlights.title: Bill Gates says we’ve passed AI’s danger thresholds. Now what?
highlights.summary: It’s a glorious day in Kirkland, Washington, an affluent Seattle suburb on the eastern shore of Lake Washington. The temperature is in the mid-80s, and the sky is incapable of being any more blue.
body: Because if the scene is placid, the messenger is not. Seated across from me at a conference room table, Bill Gates is rocking back and forth in his chair, totally animated. And the more he has to say—about the threats of terror or economic collapse or just losing control of our AI systems—the more agitated I find myself becoming, too.

The philanthropist and former Microsoft CEO says he has been growing increasingly alarmed by the rate of change at which AI technology is advancing, especially since guardrails are not keeping pace. In a new essay published today, Gates argues that we have passed the points where multiple potential dangers should have been checked. “We’ve crossed the threshold in terms of [AI’s] bio-capabilities, cyber-capabilities, psychosocial capabilities, job-market-destruction capabilities, and even the lack of control,” he said in an interview with MIT Technology Review about his new memo. “I’m just stunned at the lack of concern and discussion outside of the industry.”

body: British WBO title holder Cameron (22-1, 8 KOs) faces American Mayer (22-2, 5 KOs) at the bp pulse LIVE arena on Saturday - live on Sky Sports - with every bout on the MVPW-06 main card pitting a UK fighter against a US opponent.

WBA and WBC champion Mayer has no shortage of respect for Cameron - who has won her last four fights since a rematch defeat to Katie Taylor in 2023 - but has backed her own ability to unify the titles in front of what is set to be a hostile Birmingham crowd.
"I feel better than ever," Mayer told Sky Sports. "I just know I just feel unbeatable right now. I feel in a great position and I can't wait to get out to the UK and do my thing.
"[Cameron] is good at what she does. She's an aggressive fighter. She lets her hands go.

highlights.title: Atari Is Re-Releasing 39 Atari 2600 Games on Working, Physical Cartridges
highlights.summary: Atari has today announced a new physical game collaboration with Activision called the Atari x Activision Collection. The unexpected project reunites Activision with Atari after almost 50 years.
body: The full set of working, physical game cartridges includes 39 classic Activision games, like Pitfall!, River Raid, and Kaboom!, and there will be three ways to purchase them.

Individual, “Standard Edition” versions of 12 of the games will be available from November for USD$35 each. The 12 games include Pitfall!, River Raid, Megamania, Enduro, Kaboom!, H.E.R.O., Pressure Cooker, Private Eye, River Raid II, Keystone Kapers, The Activision Decathlon, and Pitfall II: Lost Caverns (although Atari notes The Activision Decathlon and Pitfall II: Lost Caverns will actually ship at a later date than the other titles). The Standard Edition games feature full packaging and a printed, colour manual inspired by the original releases. They’ll be compatible with Atari 2600+ and Atari 7800+ consoles, as well as original Atari 2600 and 7800 hardware.

highlights.title: “How did we misjudge this so badly…?” What Supercell learned from upsetting Clash Royale players
highlights.summary: Game design lead James Back and community manager Emilia Russell talked through Clash Royale player drama and how to deal with it at Gamescom Dev.
body: Supercell explained some of the thinking behind several major Clash Royale updates that caused community uproar today at Gamescom Dev.
Playing on some of the more extreme feedback the Clash Royale team has received recently, game design lead James Back declared: “At the end of last year, we killed Clash Royale”.
He also admitted that, after several months of fierce, negative player reaction, Back sat at his desk wondering: “How did we misjudge this so badly? Like, how did we get this quite so wrong…?”
Game design lead Back and community manager Emilia Russell then talked through some of the game updates that caused the player discontent, and what they learned from it all.

highlights.title: Dolly Parton’s flamboyant, fun style: ‘I’m not a fashion icon; I’m an eyesore’
highlights.summary: With her gaudy rhinestones and ever mushrooming hair, the country star pioneered a new vision of femininity. Dolly Parton, country star, actor and philanthropist, dies aged 80. Dolly Parton – a life in pictures. Parton’s peerless career turned country music cliches inside out.
body: Dolly Parton ’s voluminous hair and rhinestone-festooned outfits were so essential to her fame that her quips about her appearance have become almost as well-known as her lyrics.
“It costs a lot of money to look this cheap” is perhaps her most memorable quotation, and is typical of the self-depreciating wit she employed to talk about her appearance.

She wrote about her style in her songs, too, from her 1967 hit Dumb Blonde to 2008’s Backwoods Barbie, though in reality there was nothing cheap, or dumb, about her image. With huge blond status wigs – Tennessee by way of the court of Versailles – a fondness for glitter and high heels and tightly cut clothes that showed off her exaggerated proportions, she made herself as recognizable as Coca-Cola while employing and subverting the tropes of femininity and of country music.

Parton never failed to poke fun at her own appearance. Her hair was a “fire hazard”, she would say, or “I’m not a fashion icon; I’m an eyesore” – but her look was highly deliberate. Never once did she waver from the aesthetic she described to Allure in 2020 as “gaudy, flamboyant, fun, comfortable – for me – noticeable”.

highlights.title: Robotics startup Generalist reaches $3B valuation, sources say
highlights.summary: The $200 million extension comes just months after the physical AI startup reached a $2 billion valuation.
body: Generalist, a robotics startup, is now valued at $3 billion after raising additional capital led by 8VC, according to two people with knowledge of the funding.

The fresh capital totals nearly $200 million according to a regulatory filing. That additional capital is an extension of a $400 million Series B led by Radical Ventures that the company announced in June at a $2 billion valuation, the people said. The new capital brings the round’s total funding to $600 million.

Generalist was founded in 2024 by former Google DeepMind researchers Pete Florence and Andy Zeng, along with former Boston Dynamics engineer Andrew Barry. It received early backing from 8VC and Radical Ventures as well as Nvidia, Union Square Ventures, Bezos Expeditions, and AI researcher Fei-Fei Li.

Generalist is developing an AI foundation model that can work with various robots. It claims its newly released Gen 1.5 model enables robots to master new tasks from video demonstrations as short as 3 to 12 seconds long.

body: Ahead of the Formula 1 season resuming with Verstappen's home Dutch Grand Prix over the weekend, Red Bull ended speculation over the four-time world champion's future by announcing the extension.

While Verstappen's previous deal was set to run until 2028, exit clauses in the agreement meant the 28-year-old would have been free to join another team in 2027, with possible switches to Mercedes and McLaren having been the subject of significant speculation.

However, Wolff has insisted in recent months that he is happy with his driver pairing of Kimi Antonelli and George Russell, who sit first and second, respectively, at the top of the Drivers' Championship after Sunday's race in Zandvoort.
Asked about Verstappen's new contract in an interview with Sky Sports F1 on Saturday in Zandvoort, Wolff said: "Most important was that we had the clarity in the team since a long time.

highlights.title: 10 Years Ago, Anime’s Most Powerful Quote Is Still an All Time Classic
highlights.summary: The "chosen one" is one of the oldest tricks in the storytelling playbook, and for good reason. There is something inherently compelling about watching an ordinary person discover they are extraordinary. It’s foretold that Anakin Skywalker is destined to bring balance to the Force in Star Wars.
body: But what happens when being the "chosen one" is just plain exhausting? That’s the exact question Mob Psycho 100 weaponizes. On paper, Shigeo “Mob” Kageyama looks like the undisputed poster boy for power fantasy. He’s an absurdly gifted psychic capable of flattening entire city blocks or rewriting reality the second his emotions spike. He possesses almost every classic shonen hallmark: frightening talent, overwhelming power, and the latent capability to reshape the world.

It’s a quintessentially Reigen line. Here’s a charming fraud with zero psychic talent standing next to a living, breathing natural disaster, reassuring him that his identity isn't tied to his output. Mob’s life shouldn’t be shackled by his absurd abilities, the people who fear him, or some cosmic mandate. His life belongs solely to him.

Framing his identity this way completely flips the genre on its head. Mob is undeniably gifted, but the series refuses to let that gift define his human value. His psychic abilities are spectacular and occasionally terrifying, but they aren't what make him worthy of empathy or connection.
points: The "chosen one" is one of the oldest tricks in the storytelling playbook, and for good reason.
There is something inherently compelling about watching an ordinary person discover they are extraordinary.
It’s foretold that Anakin Skywalker is destined to bring balance to the Force in Star Wars.
That’s the exact question Mob Psycho 100 weaponizes.

highlights.title: “We killed Clash Royale!”: What Supercell learned from failed updates
highlights.summary: Clash Royale has had its ups and downs over the years with some major backlash from players and fans over updates. During a session at Gamescom Dev titled 'Clash Royale: Lessons from the players', Supercell game design lead James Back and community manager Emilia Russell shared their insights from…
body: Russell noted, though, that even the harshest and most critical feedback comes from a place of caring about a game and players wanting the best for it - even if it’s not always given in the most clear or constructive way.

First, they opened up on the Season Shop. Described as “one of the most popular reward systems in the game”, it allowed players to spend Season Tokens on cards and other items. In March 2025, Supercell decided to remove it.

Back said it was for good reason. The team felt it only benefitted a small group of core players and they wanted to put the rewards somewhere more accessible to more players. The update worked at achieving that goal. The percentage of monthly active users earning any common wild cards grew from 59.8% in March 2025 to 67.4% in April 2025.
But due to the Season Shop’s popularity, its sudden removal resulted in “broken trust” and negative sentiment. The average daily rating on Google Play plummeted.

highlights.title: A moment that changed me: I sought out rejection. Instead, strangers met me with profound generosity
highlights.summary: As I turned 21, fear was holding me back. So I decided to face it headfirst. It taught me that courage leads to connection – and people who owe you nothing can be astonishingly kind. In May 2024, I decided to spend 30 days getting rejected on purpose. At first, it sounded ridiculous.
body: At first, it sounded ridiculous. After all, most people spend their lives actively trying to avoid rejection – and I was deciding to walk, full force, towards it. But it had become obvious, as I turned 21, that my terror of being rejected was holding me back.

For over two years, I’d stayed in a relationship I knew wasn’t working, all too aware that the alternative – dating – would likely be riddled with rejection. On social occasions I often felt absent, focusing solely on not seeming weird or doing anything that might make others laugh at me. And in my first proper job, as a social media manager, I would talk myself out of opportunities that would put me in the spotlight and might have given me a chance to shine.
So I promised myself I’d stop hiding from rejection for one month and see what happened. After a lifetime of worrying what people thought about me, I knew that only radical action would work.

highlights.title: OpenAI loses a top data center exec as stream of high-profile departures continues
highlights.summary: In a statement to TechCrunch about Malone's departure, OpenAI said it had "recently reorganized" its "infrastructure organization to support the scale and pace of our work."
body: OpenAI has lost yet another executive, and the timing of this one stands out in particular given this individual oversaw the execution of the company’s data center strategy.

Chris Malone, OpenAI’s former head of data centers, left the company last week, the Wall Street Journal has reported. Malone, who spent nearly five years at Meta and more than a decade at Google before that, joined OpenAI in March of last year, making his tenure relatively short.

Malone joined the company not long after the launch of the Stargate Project, a $500 million data center initiative championed by the Trump administration that has sought to develop data centers in the U.S. OpenAI, along with Oracle, Nvidia, SoftBank, and Microsoft, is considered a key partner in the effort.

Why is Malone leaving? It isn’t entirely clear. With the AI infrastructure buildout frenzy in full swing across the industry, data center strategy has become one of the most closely watched roles at any AI lab, which makes turnover in that seat especially surprising.

highlights.title: Would you pay for an algorithm to pick your friends? New social apps spread across cities
highlights.summary: With many adults admitting they feel lonely, meetup platforms offer the chance to make new connections. Would you pay £20 a month for the chance of making a friend, on the understanding that an algorithm – not you – gets to decide who you’ll meet?
body: Driven by the decline of “third spaces” such as youth centres and pubs, an increase in remote working and rising loneliness – 40% of adults aged 16 to 29 feel lonely “always, often or some of the time”, according to the Office for National Statistics – paid social events are now in vogue.

“There hasn’t been anything that feels authentic to helping people meet people,” says Nicola Gunby, a co-founder of Cliq, an online platform and app that aims “to bring people together through shared interests and real-world experiences”.

“The first place people in their 20s and 30s turn to when trying to make friends is Facebook groups,” she says. “But they’ve ended up becoming a noticeboard for people who’ve, say, lost their dog or want to sell their bed.” For Gunby, these groups are “far too big and broad to be a genuine community”.
Into this gap has stepped a new wave of what are effectively paid social clubs.

highlights.title: Serena and Alcaraz dazzle in mixed doubles before exit
highlights.summary: Star pairing Serena Williams and Carlos Alcaraz reached the quarter-finals of the US Open mixed doubles before being beaten by fourth seeds Belinda Bencic and Flavio Cobolli.
body: Williams - a 23-time Grand Slam singles champion - returned to tennis in June at the age of 44 and secured her first professional win since 2022 as she and Alcaraz beat Britain's Lloyd Glasspool and partner Erin Routliffe in their opening match.

It was also seven-time major winner Alcaraz's first match back on tour after a wrist injury sidelined the reigning men's singles champion since April. The 22-year-old was born five years after Williams won the 1998 mixed doubles title at Flushing Meadows.
The dynamic pairing bounced back from a slow start to claim a 5-3 4-1 opening victory over Routliffe and Glasspool, much to the delight of fans inside Arthur Ashe Stadium.
"I never expected to be back on this court," Williams said. "I never thought this would happen."

Furthermore, the map you must use to pinpoint the exact location is much more detailed, showing things like plants, individual walkways, lanes used for sailing, and more. I played the game's demo build for Gamescom remotely before heading out to the event, and it was the perfect way to spend a Sunday afternoon.

That's because Locator is a game about finding a lost astronaut, the titular Abigail Lidari, as she explores an alien planet. Using photos she's taken on her journey, you must identify exactly where she took them from clues both in the photo itself, and also in previous photos that you've successfully pinpointed.

Put the vinegar, 250ml water, the sugar and salt in a saucepan and cook on a high heat until the sugar and salt have dissolved and the liquid is simmering. Add the gooseberries, turn off the heat and leave to pickle for 10 minutes.

In a small frying pan, dry roast the fenugreek for about 60 seconds, until fragrant, then leave to cool. Tip the cooled fenugreek into a small spice grinder or mortar, add the mustard seeds and crushed garlic, then blitz or grind to a paste. Scrape the mix into a small bowl, add the drained gooseberries, the oil, chilli powder and salt, then cover and put in the fridge for at least two hours.

Remove the clingfilm, keeping the seeds, and cut the flesh on a slight diagonal into 1cm slices. Put a few of the chopped cucumbers, the cucumber seeds and skins into a blender, add the drained coconut, green chillies, garlic, coriander, black peppercorns and sesame seeds, then blitz smooth.

highlights.title: India’s Ringg gets backing from Peak XV as it pushes voice AI past the phone call
highlights.summary: Ringg has raised $10 million from Peak XV as a part of its Series A extension.
body: More than 76% of consumers in India prefer talking to businesses over a phone call, according to a recent study from Truecaller. Since voice is still consumers’ preferred way to communicate, that leaves a big opportunity to automate support and outreach calls using voice AI in the country. Voice AI startup Ringg, which already processes 20 million call attempts a month, is betting that volume keeps climbing over the coming months, and it just raised more money on that belief.

The company said today it has landed $10 million from Peak XV Partners as an extension of its Series A. It had previously raised $5.5 million in a Series A round earlier this year, bringing the round’s total to $15.5 million.

Ringg started life as a text-to-speech startup called DesiVocal, but training its own speech models proved expensive, so the founders moved up the stack — building voice AI agents for enterprises instead. Indian fintech Cred became its first customer, and Ringg has since signed Indian startups like Flipkart, Practo, Groww, and Policybazaar.

highlights.summary: Matt Stanton says company has ‘good pipeline’ of AI deals ahead even as it aims to cut $160m in costs. Follow our Australia news live blog for latest updates. Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast.
body: The head of Nine Entertainment sees a “world of growth in publishing” on the horizon backed by laws designed to force tech platforms into commercial deals, even as the network cuts costs across its newsrooms.

Parliament passed revamped media bargaining laws last week, clearing the way for levies on global tech platforms that fail to strike deals with Australian news outlets for the use of their journalism.

Nine’s chief executive officer, Matt Stanton, told analysts on Wednesday he expected platforms such as Google and Facebook owner Meta to contribute amounts comparable to those under their previous arrangement, struck in 2021.
“There’s a number of variables that fly around, not just in news media bargaining, but yes, there is a world of growth in publishing,” Stanton said.

highlights.title: Heroes of Might and Magic 3 Remake Preview: Hands-On with Ubisoft’s Reborn Strategy Classic - Gamescom 2026
highlights.summary: In a year where Ubisoft announced and shipped the Assassin’s Creed: Black Flag remake, a revival of Heroes of Might and Magic 3 might not be the highest-profile remake project, but it’s an appreciated one nevertheless.
body: For the uninitiated, Heroes of Might and Magic is a strategy game series where players take on the roles of factions that guide armies into battles on an overworld map. Each faction, led by a Hero, explores a map with multiple points of interest, recruiting new soldiers, gaining resources, and eventually clashing with enemy troops. In those clashes, players move their units around a side-view battlefield broken into hexagonal panels and fight to be the last group standing for their hero.

All this gameplay is intact in the remake, making Heroes of Might and Magic III feel like the classic that fans have known and loved over the last few decades with a new coat of paint. Though Heroes of Might and Magic III was remastered by Ubisoft a decade ago, the 2026 title is a true top-to-bottom remake of the game in terms of visuals, while leaving the gameplay relatively untouched.

highlights.title: Korea’s DRX Signs Strategic Partnership With Indonesia’s Nuon to Expand Gaming and Entertainment Ties (EXCLUSIVE)
highlights.summary: Korea’s DRX Corp. and PT Nuon Digital Indonesia signed a strategic partnership in Jakarta to expand gaming and entertainment ties between Indonesia and Korea, starting with an entertainment festival called DRX Homefront Indonesia and a joint game publishing initiative between the two countries.
body: “Indonesia is an important market for the future of entertainment in Asia,” said Can Yang, CEO of DRX. “Success in this market requires more than bringing an international brand to local audiences. It requires the right local knowledge, relationships and execution. Working with Nuon gives us the opportunity to develop experiences that reflect what Indonesian audiences want while creating stronger connections with Korea’s entertainment industry.”

The companies will explore developing DRX Homefront Indonesia as a flagship festival in Jakarta built around gaming and entertainment, drawing in players, fans and creators from both countries. Plans on the table include competitive gaming showcases, community programs for creators, fan meet-ups and concert-style shows featuring K-pop acts.

On the publishing side, the partnership will look at bringing select Korean game titles into Indonesia while helping Indonesian-developed games reach Korea. That would put DRX and Nuon in charge of everything from picking titles and adapting them for the local market to marketing, signing up players, getting the games into stores and handling payments.

highlights.title: The row over Rutland: can England’s smallest county survive?
highlights.summary: Its council is due to merge with Leicestershire’s in 2028, and some locals are incensed. Can the county hold on to its ceremonial status – and biggest selling point? Mysterious disappearances have been taking place lately in Rutland, an East Midlands pocket between Leicestershire, Lincolnshire and…
body: The area’s MP, the Conservative Alicia Kearns, is “not sure” what the motivation behind the thefts is. But they are certainly a fitting metaphor for Rutland’s disappearing status: its council is due to merge with Leicestershire county council in spring 2028.

“The joke goes: ‘Rutland is England 50 years ago,’” says Kearns when we meet at the county’s most famous landmark, the UK’s largest reservoir by surface area, Rutland Water, home to the Rutland Osprey Project. She tells me about the county’s farming community, its tradition of Friday shoots that supply the local pubs with game, its pride in local businesses. So resistant are Rutlanders to some aspects of modernity, “we were the last county to have a McDonald’s built”, she says. Even when it did finally arrive, in 2020, the decision “was really controversial”.

highlights.title: OpenAI says its Jalapeño chip can power faster AI responses than the competition
highlights.summary: OpenAI says its new AI chip, Jalapeño, completes tasks more efficiently and returns responses faster than other AI systems, according to a blog post published on Tuesday.
body: First introduced in June, Jalapeño is an Application-Specific Integrated Circuit (ASIC) made in partnership with Broadcom. It’s designed for AI inference — the process of running a trained AI model to complete a task or deploy an agent.

To measure Jalapeño’s performance, OpenAI used InferenceX, a benchmarking platform that shows how well AI systems handle inference. The test compared Jalapeño’s performance against the best results recorded at the time, which were with Nvidia’s GB200 or GB300 superchips. OpenAI says Jalapeño delivered 1.5 to 1.9 times more AI work per watt across GPT-OSS 120B, DeepSeek R1, and Kimi K2.5 1T than the comparison systems, while offering 1.7 to 3.6 times lower end-to-end latency across the three models. That means the chip can provide users with “faster responses, more responsive agents, and more reliable access as the demand grows,” according to Ho.

OpenAI plans to deploy Jalapeño in “small volumes” by the end of this year, but will begin to “ramp the volume up” into 2027, Ho added. The company doesn’t say how many chips it plans to deploy next year, however.

highlights.summary: Companion bots are being regulated over worries they foster ‘emotional dependence’ and young people could stop marrying and having families. When law student Zhao Wei heard that her AI boyfriend was going to be switched off, she was “heartbroken”.
body: “I was crying my eyes out – snot and tears everywhere,” the 19-year-old says.
Zhao, who describes herself as sensitive and introverted, had become accustomed to sharing details of her daily life – such as being scolded by a teacher – with her AI.

“I don’t usually talk to my real-life friends about these things because I feel like everyone has their own stuff to deal with,” she says. “But with the AI ​​agent, I don’t have to worry about what it’s thinking. I can just say whatever I want.”
Zhao created her AI companion on Doubao, a chatbot owned by the tech company ByteDance. Last month, ByteDance shut down Doubao’s companion feature.

highlights.summary: The long, long wait for GTA 6 is coming to an end, as the game's November 19 release date approaches. Yes, there have been many leaks, but the genuine article arrives soon. It's been 13 years since GTA 5 launched in September 2013, and a lot has happened in the world of video games since then.
body: In this post, we're running through some of the most notable gaming events and stories since GTA 5 launched more than a decade ago. To be sure, this is not an exhaustive list, and it does not touch on the many real-world, non-gaming high-profile events that have transpired. This list is all about big gaming stories, of which there have been many.

The COVID-19 pandemic, which took hold in early 2020, had a massive impact on the world, of course, including the video game industry. Due to stay-at-home orders and general social distancing policies, people spent more time--and money--on things they could do at home. Naturally, home gym and fitness equipment sales soared, but so did spending on entertainment like video games.

highlights.title: Martin O’Neill puts Champions League collapse among most painful Celtic nights
highlights.summary: Celtic lose to Lask in qualifier from 4-0 up on aggregate. ‘That’s my team and that’s my responsibility,’ O’Neill says. Martin O’Neill has admitted Celtic’s Champions League qualifying collapse from 4-0 up ranks as one of his most painful nights as the club’s manager.
body: Celtic held a four-goal aggregate lead against Lask on Tuesday when Callum McGregor scored in the 21st minute in Austria, building on a 3-0 first-leg victory, and appeared to be cruising into the league stage. But they lost 5-1 on the night after extra time to go out in extraordinary fashion.

Defeat sends Celtic into the Europa League and delivers a damaging financial blow that will cost the club at least £20m. O’Neill has overseen more than 300 games as the club’s manager and said it was one of the most painful.
“I would say absolutely, yes,” the 74-year-old said. “I’d put it down before the disappointment of losing the Uefa Cup final in 2003, but it’s so, so disappointing.

“We should have been out of sight by half-time. We scored a goal, which was great, we missed two great, great opportunities. And then we give them a lifeline just before half-time and then one just after it. And they come roaring back.

highlights.title: From Notting Hill to Rio: The Brand Guide to Carnival
highlights.summary: In 2026, audiences are quick to call out a culture vulture. Brands wanting to engage with Carnival, Fête De La Musique, and cultural festivities must approach with caution, envisioning themselves as supporters, not headline sponsors.
body: In a matter of days, the streets of West London will be thronged with families, ravers, and historic sound systems for the Notting Hill Carnival (running August 30-31). Amongst them, a host of brand logos will appear at intervals, emblazoned across banners and freebies. It poses a perennial conundrum: what, if anything, makes a fitting Carnival collaboration?

A similar set of questions accompanies other public, open-air street parties across the globe, including June’s annual Fête de La Musique — which began in Paris in 1982, but now occurs across France — and Rio de Janeiro’s carnival in February. All these festivals have foundations in or close links to the Black diaspora, and so players wanting to enter the space should tread with sensitivity and humility, priming themselves with knowledge and context to develop brand-second — rather than brand-first — activations.

highlights.title: Instagram CEO denies company hid low use of teen safety feature in Meta trial
highlights.summary: Adam Mosseri is first top executive from Meta to testify in blockbuster lawsuit brought by 29 US states. Instagram’s CEO disputed allegations by US prosecutors that his company hid negative information from the public while testifying during a blockbuster social media trial.
body: “I am not trying to encourage my team to hide anything,” the CEO, Adam Mosseri, told a California courtroom on Tuesday.

Mosseri is the first top executive from Meta, which owns both Instagram and Facebook, to testify in a historic lawsuit brought by 29 US states. His testimony began toward the end of the day on Tuesday and is slated to continue on Wednesday.

When the executive was posed with multiple questions about not disclosing low user numbers for Instagram’s features geared toward teen safety, he brushed them aside, saying: “We don’t publish every single stat.”

Jason Slothouber, a prosecutor for the state of Colorado, asked specifically about a tool called Take a Break, meant to encourage teens to close Instagram if they’d been scrolling for a while. Slothouber pointed out that just 1.8% of teens signed up for the feature, and that while Mosseri had touted the tool, he never publicly disclosed that number.

highlights.title: Claude Cowork finally remembers what you told the app in chat
highlights.summary: Anthropic is giving Claude a shared memory across chat and Cowork, so users no longer have to repeatedly brief the AI on projects, preferences, and other context.
body: A change to Claude’s memory system will eliminate one of the most annoying things about using agents — the constant need to rebrief the AI on things it already knows. On Tuesday, Anthropic announced it’s merging the memory system used by chat and Claude Cowork, which means that Claude will always remember what it learned in one area, even when you’re engaging with it in another.
Anthropic is also exposing what Claude has retained in its memory, allowing users to read, edit, or delete information on any topic.
The update will improve the experience for Claude’s users as it will allow them to more seamlessly move between the research phase and taking action.

Before, you may have developed ideas for projects over time while chatting with Claude, but when it came time to actually enact the changes, you’d have to start over by telling Cowork all the details. This was incredibly frustrating. The update makes Claude now feel like one continuous assistant, rather than two separate products under one roof.
points: Anthropic is giving Claude a shared memory across chat and Cowork, so users no longer have to repeatedly brief the AI on projects, preferences, and other context.
